source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #362 (branch fix/344-coalescing-panic at head f7faf699736f55d848b258fb3934dd170e80e67a — the #344 change (the core optimizer recomputes the local coalescing pairs after the GVN cache rewrite) on current main 6ec1ae13b5aa9d6886cdb0e89a87bccfee7bda20 (PR #352); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45649719958, 45649915040 and 45649992051 against the branch and pull-request run 45647683493, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #362 (#344, the core optimizer recomputes the local coalescing pairs after the GVN cache rewrite), measured on the branch head f7faf69, which is current main 6ec1ae13b5aa9d6886cdb0e89a87bccfee7bda20 (PR #352) plus the single implementation commit, so no merge was needed and the measured tree is the branch head itself. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone four times (workflow_dispatch runs 45649620006, 45649658859, 45649743600 and 45649763229 on main at 6ec1ae13b5aa9d6886cdb0e89a87bccfee7bda20; all four runs pass the gate, and the main control is byte-identical to the checked-in baseline on the sixteen core series and on the baseline configuration, and below it on the twelve component-linking series, whose baselines were retained above the measurements when PR #354 shrank those configurations). This PR's own delta against the main control is present in every configuration that links the telomere library and absent from the baseline configuration, which retains no runtime code: release stripped file +208 B (core, core-aot), +192 B (core-nosimd, wasi, wasi-threads) and +176 B (component, core-jit) and stripped .text +96 B in each of the seven; release-size stripped file +144 B and stripped .text +64 B in each of the seven — the one added compute_coalescible_local_pairs call in the optimizer pipeline. Following the established practice of re-baselining growth only, the sixteen core series are re-baselined to the branch measurements and the component-linking baselines are retained, so the retained baselines sit above the branch measurements (release stripped file by 112,552 B (component), 112,536 B (wasi) and 112,520 B (wasi-threads)). Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the four branch samples and across the four main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release component stripped file series at +11.42% (2,433,656 B to 2,711,648 B), unchanged because that series' baseline is retained. The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
